questionText: Which of the following best describes demand forecasting in inventory management?
options: The process of counting physical stock on hand
The process of estimating future customer demand for products
The process of ordering goods from suppliers
The process of evaluating supplier performance

questionText: Which forecasting method uses historical data patterns to predict future demand?
options: Qualitative forecasting
Judgmental forecasting
Time series forecasting
Market research forecasting

questionText: A moving average forecast is best described as:
options: A forecast based solely on expert opinion
An average of demand over a fixed number of the most recent periods
A forecast adjusted by seasonal indices only
A regression-based estimate of future demand

questionText: Which of the following is a qualitative forecasting method?
options: Exponential smoothing
Linear regression
Delphi method
Moving average

questionText: Exponential smoothing assigns weights to historical data in which of the following ways?
options: Equal weights to all historical periods
Higher weights to older data and lower weights to recent data
Higher weights to more recent data and lower weights to older data
Weights based solely on seasonal patterns

questionText: If the smoothing constant (α) in exponential smoothing is close to 1, the forecast will:
options: React slowly to changes in demand
Ignore recent demand completely
React very quickly to recent changes in demand
Produce a constant forecast regardless of demand

questionText: Which of the following measures is used to evaluate forecast accuracy?
options: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)
Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD)
Reorder Point (ROP)
Safety stock level

questionText: Mean Squared Error (MSE) penalizes large forecast errors more heavily than MAD because it:
options: Divides errors by the number of periods
Takes the absolute value of errors
Squares the forecast errors before averaging
Uses only the most recent period's error

questionText: A tracking signal in forecasting is used to:
options: Determine the optimal order quantity
Monitor whether a forecasting model remains accurate over time
Calculate safety stock levels
Identify the best supplier for procurement

questionText: Which type of demand pattern shows a consistent upward or downward movement over time?
options: Seasonal pattern
Cyclical pattern
Random variation
Trend pattern

questionText: Seasonal demand patterns are characterized by:
options: Random fluctuations with no predictable timing
Repetitive demand fluctuations tied to specific time periods within a year
A long-term upward or downward movement in demand
Demand that is perfectly constant across all periods

questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about the Delphi forecasting method?
options: It relies exclusively on mathematical models
It uses structured rounds of expert opinion to reach a consensus forecast
It is based on regression analysis of historical sales data
It requires point-of-sale data from retail outlets

questionText: Linear regression in forecasting is primarily used to:
options: Calculate the reorder point for inventory
Identify the relationship between demand and one or more independent variables
Determine safety stock based on lead time variability
Assign weights to different historical periods

questionText: A company's forecast for Month 6 is 200 units, but actual demand was 240 units. The forecast error is:
options: -40 units
40 units
200 units
440 units

questionText: Which forecasting approach is most appropriate when a new product has no historical demand data?
options: Time series analysis
Exponential smoothing
Moving average
Qualitative methods such as market surveys

questionText: The Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) expresses forecast accuracy as:
options: The average of squared errors
The sum of all forecast errors divided by number of periods
The average absolute error as a percentage of actual demand
The difference between the highest and lowest forecast values

questionText: Collaborative Planning, Forecasting, and Replenishment (CPFR) improves demand forecasting by:
options: Eliminating the need for safety stock entirely
Sharing demand information between supply chain partners
Using only internal sales data for all forecasts
Replacing all qualitative methods with quantitative ones

questionText: Which of the following statements about forecast error is correct?
options: A forecast error of zero means the model is always accurate
Positive forecast errors mean the forecast exceeded actual demand
Negative forecast errors mean the forecast was lower than actual demand
Forecast errors should always be ignored in inventory planning

questionText: A three-period moving average uses the demand figures of:
options: The three oldest periods in the data set
Any three randomly selected historical periods
The three most recent periods of historical demand
The three periods with the highest demand values

questionText: Forecast bias occurs when:
options: Forecast errors are randomly distributed around zero
There is a consistent tendency to over-forecast or under-forecast
The forecasting model uses too many historical periods
Seasonal adjustments are applied incorrectly

questionText: Which of the following demand components refers to unpredictable fluctuations not explained by trend or seasonality?
options: Cyclical variation
Trend
Random variation
Seasonal variation

questionText: A company notices its tracking signal has exceeded the control limit. This most likely means:
options: The forecast model is performing well and requires no changes
The safety stock level needs to be reduced
The forecasting model may be biased and needs review
The order quantity should be increased immediately

questionText: Which of the following best describes point-of-sale (POS) data in forecasting?
options: Data generated from supplier invoices
Real-time demand data captured at the time and location of purchase
Demand estimates based on historical production records
Data collected through annual customer surveys

questionText: Demand variability in forecasting refers to:
options: The average demand level across all periods
The degree to which actual demand fluctuates around the forecast
The total demand over the planning horizon
The number of periods used in the moving average

questionText: When using exponential smoothing, increasing the value of α will:
options: Give more weight to older observations
Reduce the responsiveness of the forecast to recent demand changes
Give more weight to recent observations and less to older ones
Eliminate random variation from the forecast

questionText: Which of the following is a limitation of the moving average forecasting method?
options: It cannot be computed using historical data
It reacts too quickly to every single demand observation
It treats all periods in the average equally, regardless of recency
It requires knowledge of lead time demand

questionText: Safety stock levels are most directly influenced by:
options: The forecasting method chosen
Variability in demand and lead time
The number of suppliers used
The type of warehousing system employed

questionText: Which statement best describes a causal forecasting model?
options: It relies on expert panels to estimate future demand
It forecasts demand based on its relationship with external variables like economic indicators
It calculates demand as a fixed percentage of past sales
It uses only internal production records to estimate demand

questionText: A high Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) value indicates:
options: The forecast is highly accurate
There is little variability between forecast and actual demand
There are large forecast errors on average
The smoothing constant is set too low

questionText: Which of the following best describes "forecast horizon"?
options: The number of historical periods used to calculate the forecast
The length of time into the future for which a forecast is made
The acceptable range of forecast error
The maximum inventory level allowed in the warehouse

questionText: The Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) model minimizes:
options: Total revenue from sales
Only ordering costs
The sum of total ordering and holding costs
Only holding costs

questionText: Which of the following is an assumption of the basic EOQ model?
options: Demand varies significantly across periods
Lead time is variable and uncertain
Demand is constant and known with certainty
Shortages are allowed and backordered

questionText: In the EOQ formula Q* = √(2DS/H), the variable "D" represents:
options: The unit purchase price of the item
The annual demand for the item
The cost of holding one unit for one year
The ordering cost per order

questionText: Holding costs in inventory management include which of the following?
options: Cost of placing a purchase order
Transportation cost from supplier to warehouse
Cost of capital tied up in inventory and storage costs
Supplier invoice processing fees

questionText: As order quantity increases in the EOQ model, holding costs will:
options: Decrease proportionally
Remain unchanged
Increase because average inventory level rises
Decrease because fewer orders are placed

questionText: The Reorder Point (ROP) in inventory management is defined as:
options: The maximum inventory level before disposal
The inventory level at which a new order should be placed
The quantity ordered each time an order is placed
The total demand for an item over one year

questionText: Which of the following correctly represents the formula for Reorder Point (ROP) without safety stock?
options: ROP = Annual Demand × Lead Time
ROP = Average Daily Demand × Lead Time in Days
ROP = EOQ / Lead Time
ROP = Holding Cost × Lead Time

questionText: Safety stock is added to the reorder point primarily to:
options: Reduce the order quantity below EOQ
Eliminate the need for demand forecasting
Protect against stockouts caused by demand or lead time variability
Decrease the frequency of orders placed

questionText: Which of the following increases the Economic Order Quantity?
options: Decrease in annual demand
Decrease in ordering cost
Increase in annual demand
Increase in holding cost

questionText: The average inventory under the basic EOQ model (with no safety stock) is:
options: Equal to the order quantity Q
Equal to half the order quantity Q/2
Equal to the reorder point
Equal to annual demand divided by order quantity

questionText: The number of orders placed per year in the EOQ model is calculated as:
options: EOQ divided by holding cost
Annual demand multiplied by order quantity
Annual demand divided by the order quantity
Order quantity multiplied by ordering cost

questionText: Which inventory cost increases as order quantity decreases?
options: Holding cost
Purchase price per unit
Annual ordering cost
Storage space cost

questionText: A stockout occurs when:
options: Inventory exceeds the maximum allowable level
An order arrives before the reorder point is reached
Demand cannot be fulfilled due to insufficient inventory
The reorder point is set too high

questionText: The service level in inventory management refers to:
options: The speed at which orders are processed by the supplier
The probability of not experiencing a stockout during the lead time
The ratio of on-hand inventory to total warehouse capacity
The percentage of orders delivered on time by suppliers

questionText: Which of the following best describes "cycle stock"?
options: Inventory held as a buffer against demand uncertainty
Inventory that is obsolete and ready for disposal
The portion of inventory that results from replenishment ordering activity
Inventory reserved for seasonal demand peaks

questionText: A higher desired service level generally requires:
options: Lower safety stock levels
Smaller order quantities
Higher safety stock levels
Fewer reorder points

questionText: In the EOQ model, the optimal total cost curve is relatively:
options: Steep on both sides of the optimal point
Flat near the optimal point, making the model robust to small deviations
Highly sensitive to small changes in order quantity
Always minimized at the lowest possible order quantity

questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about the Total Cost (TC) in the EOQ model?
options: TC is minimized when ordering cost equals purchase cost
TC is minimized when ordering cost equals holding cost
TC is minimized when holding cost is zero
TC increases continuously as order quantity rises

questionText: Lead time variability in inventory management primarily affects:
options: The EOQ calculation
The determination of safety stock and reorder point
The annual ordering frequency
The holding cost per unit

questionText: Which inventory reliability measure expresses the fraction of demand satisfied directly from stock?
options: Reorder point
Economic order quantity
Fill rate
Cycle time

questionText: Which of the following statements about safety stock is correct?
options: Safety stock is consumed during normal demand periods
Safety stock increases the average cycle stock
Safety stock provides a buffer against demand and lead time uncertainty
Safety stock reduces the need for a reorder point

questionText: The "quantity discount" model modifies the basic EOQ by:
options: Eliminating ordering costs from the total cost equation
Considering the impact of lower unit prices at higher order quantities
Assuming demand is probabilistic rather than deterministic
Using variable lead times in the reorder point calculation

questionText: Which of the following will DECREASE the reorder point?
options: Increase in average daily demand
Increase in lead time
Decrease in safety stock
Increase in demand variability

questionText: The "bullwhip effect" in supply chains is most directly related to which inventory concept?
options: EOQ optimization
Demand variability amplification upstream in the supply chain
Safety stock elimination
Reorder point reduction

questionText: Which of the following best describes "pipeline inventory"?
options: Inventory stored in warehouses awaiting orders
Inventory in transit between supply chain nodes
Inventory reserved for seasonal demand fluctuations
Obsolete inventory pending disposal

questionText: A company that adopts a higher reorder point than necessary will most likely experience:
options: Frequent stockouts
Reduced holding costs
Excess inventory and higher holding costs
Increased ordering frequency

questionText: The "two-bin system" is an example of which inventory control approach?
options: Periodic review system
Continuous review system
Material Requirements Planning (MRP)
Just-in-Time system

questionText: Which of the following factors does NOT directly affect the EOQ calculation?
options: Annual demand
Ordering cost per order
Unit selling price to customers
Annual holding cost per unit

questionText: If a company's ordering cost doubles while all other factors remain constant, the EOQ will:
options: Double
Remain unchanged
Increase by approximately 41%
Decrease by 50%

questionText: Which of the following best describes "order cycle time"?
options: The time from placing an order to receiving it from the supplier
The time between successive order placements
The time required to process a customer order internally
The total time goods spend in the warehouse

questionText: Deterministic inventory models assume which of the following about demand?
options: Demand is probabilistic and unknown
Demand is known with certainty
Demand follows a normal distribution
Demand changes randomly from period to period

questionText: Under a fixed order quantity system with known demand, an order is triggered when:
options: A fixed time interval elapses
Inventory falls to the reorder point
The holding cost exceeds the ordering cost
The supplier sends a delivery confirmation

questionText: The Production Order Quantity (POQ) model differs from EOQ in that:
options: It assumes demand is probabilistic
It accounts for inventory being replenished gradually rather than instantaneously
It eliminates holding costs from the total cost equation
It is only applicable to service industries

questionText: In the POQ model, the maximum inventory level is less than the order quantity because:
options: Some units are damaged during production
Goods are consumed as they are produced simultaneously
The reorder point reduces the effective order size
Holding costs are subtracted from the order quantity

questionText: Which of the following is the correct formula for Economic Production Quantity (EPQ)?
options: EPQ = √(2DS/H)
EPQ = D × S / H
EPQ = √(2DH/S)

questionText: In the EPQ model, "p" represents:
options: The unit price of the product
The production rate (units per time period)
The probability of a stockout
The percentage of defective items

questionText: A fixed-period (periodic review) inventory system places orders:
options: Whenever inventory reaches the reorder point
At regular, predetermined time intervals
Only when a stockout has been detected
Based on supplier lead time recommendations

questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of the fixed-order quantity system over the periodic review system?
options: It requires less frequent monitoring of inventory levels
It is simpler to administer for multiple items simultaneously
It typically results in lower average safety stock
It is easier to coordinate deliveries of multiple items

questionText: Under a periodic review system, the "order-up-to" level (target inventory level) is determined by:
options: EOQ divided by average demand
Expected demand during the review period plus lead time, plus safety stock
Annual demand divided by the number of review periods
Reorder point multiplied by the review interval

questionText: Which of the following statements about the fixed-order quantity system is correct?
options: The quantity ordered varies from order to order
The time between orders is always constant
The order quantity remains the same each time an order is placed
Orders are placed at fixed calendar intervals regardless of inventory level

questionText: The "ABC analysis" approach to inventory management classifies items based on:
options: Their physical size and weight
Their annual consumption value relative to total inventory value
Their lead time from suppliers
Their storage location in the warehouse

questionText: "A" items in ABC analysis typically represent:
options: The largest number of SKUs but the smallest share of total value
The smallest number of SKUs but the largest share of total annual value
Items with the most variable demand
Items stored in the most accessible warehouse locations

questionText: Which of the following is a key benefit of ABC analysis in inventory management?
options: It eliminates the need for safety stock for all items
It allows managers to focus tighter controls on high-value items
It reduces lead times for all inventory categories
It replaces the need for a reorder point system

questionText: In a deterministic inventory model, the total annual inventory cost is minimized when:
options: Ordering cost is zero
Holding cost per unit is minimized
The annual ordering cost equals the annual holding cost
Order quantity equals annual demand

questionText: Which type of inventory model would be most appropriate for a manufacturer producing goods at a finite rate to meet steady demand?
options: Basic EOQ model
Probabilistic demand model
Production Order Quantity (POQ) model
Periodic review model

questionText: A company produces 500 units per day and demand is 100 units per day. If the production run lasts 10 days, what is the maximum inventory level?
options: 5,000 units
1,000 units
4,000 units
500 units

questionText: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of the basic deterministic EOQ model?
options: Constant demand rate
Instantaneous replenishment
No quantity discounts
Probabilistic lead time

questionText: The "lot-for-lot" ordering policy in inventory management means:
options: Ordering one lot per month regardless of demand
Ordering exactly the quantity demanded in each period, with no excess
Ordering the economic order quantity in each period
Ordering based on supplier minimum order requirements

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the impact of shorter lead times on inventory management?
options: They increase the required safety stock levels
They allow for lower reorder points and reduced inventory investment
They require larger order quantities to compensate
They increase total annual ordering costs

questionText: A firm uses a continuous review system with known, constant demand. Which of the following will trigger a replenishment order?
options: A predetermined calendar date is reached
Inventory on hand drops to or below the reorder point
The supplier notifies the firm that stock is available
The planning period ends and a review is conducted

questionText: Which of the following inventory costs is most directly associated with capital investment in stock?
options: Ordering cost
Shortage cost
Carrying/holding cost
Transportation cost

questionText: In the EOQ model with quantity discounts, a manager should select the order quantity that:
options: Minimizes only the purchase price per unit
Minimizes total annual cost including purchasing, ordering, and holding costs
Always equals the EOQ calculated at the lowest price
Maximizes the quantity discount received

questionText: Which of the following best describes "just-in-time" (JIT) inventory philosophy in relation to known demand?
options: Maintaining large safety stocks to avoid any disruption
Ordering and receiving inventory just as it is needed to minimize holding costs
Placing large infrequent orders to benefit from quantity discounts
Using periodic review systems exclusively for all inventory items

questionText: In a fixed-period system, which of the following poses the greatest risk?
options: Excess inventory due to over-ordering
Stockouts between review periods if demand surges unexpectedly
Increased ordering costs from frequent reviews
Inability to take advantage of quantity discounts

questionText: If demand is known and constant, safety stock in a deterministic model is:
options: Set at 50% of the average cycle stock
Equal to one week's average demand
Not required since demand is certain
Determined by the service level target

questionText: The "silver-meal heuristic" is a technique used for:
options: Calculating safety stock under uncertainty
Lot sizing when demand varies across periods
Determining the optimal number of warehouses
Selecting the best transportation mode

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes "dead stock" in inventory management?
options: Inventory currently in transit from the supplier
Stock that has been damaged during warehousing
Inventory that has not moved for an extended period and is unlikely to sell
Inventory reserved for emergency orders

questionText: The annual holding cost in EOQ is calculated as:
options: (Q/2) × H, where H is the holding cost per unit per year
(D/Q) × S, where S is the ordering cost per order
Q × D × unit purchase price
EOQ × average demand rate

questionText: Which of the following is TRUE when demand is perfectly known and constant?
options: Safety stock is essential to maintain service levels
Stockouts will occur periodically regardless of ordering policy
The inventory system can be managed with zero safety stock
The reorder point must be set above the EOQ

questionText: A company orders 500 units each time it places an order. If demand is 5,000 units per year, how many orders are placed per year?
options: 5 orders
10 orders
20 orders
25 orders

questionText: Independent demand inventory is best described as demand that is:
options: Derived directly from the production schedule of a parent item
Driven by external market forces and not directly tied to other items
Known with certainty and remains constant over time
Managed exclusively through Material Requirements Planning (MRP)

questionText: Which of the following is an example of an independent demand item?
options: A sub-assembly component used in manufacturing a finished product
A raw material required to produce a specific product
Finished goods sold directly to end customers
A fastener used exclusively in assembling a parent item

questionText: The continuous review (Q) system for independent demand is also known as:
options: The periodic order system
The fixed-time-period system
The fixed-order-quantity system
The material requirements planning system

questionText: In a continuous review system, which parameter triggers a replenishment order?
options: A fixed review interval elapses
Inventory position drops to or below the reorder point
The supplier's lead time expires
The planning horizon is reached

questionText: "Inventory position" in a continuous review system is defined as:
options: On-hand inventory minus backorders
On-hand inventory plus on-order inventory minus backorders
On-hand inventory divided by average daily demand
On-order inventory minus safety stock

questionText: Which of the following best describes the periodic review (P) system?
options: Orders are placed whenever inventory reaches the reorder point
Orders are placed at fixed time intervals for variable quantities
Order quantity is always fixed at the EOQ
Orders are placed only when a stockout occurs

questionText: In a periodic review system, which of the following increases the required safety stock compared to a continuous review system?
options: Shorter review periods reduce the uncertainty window
The uncertainty window covers both the review period and lead time
Fixed order quantities reduce demand variability
Periodic systems always have lower ordering costs

questionText: Which of the following is a major advantage of the continuous review system over the periodic review system?
options: It requires less monitoring effort
It is easier to coordinate multi-item orders from a single supplier
It generally requires lower safety stock for the same service level
It eliminates the need for reorder point calculations

questionText: "Demand during lead time" is a critical input for which inventory calculation?
options: Economic Order Quantity
Annual ordering cost
Reorder Point with safety stock
Production Order Quantity

questionText: If demand during lead time follows a normal distribution, safety stock is typically calculated as:
options: Safety stock = z × σ(lead time demand), where z is the service level z-score
Safety stock = Average demand × Lead time
Safety stock = EOQ / 2
Safety stock = Annual demand / Number of orders

questionText: A z-value of 1.65 in safety stock calculation corresponds to approximately which service level?
Which of the following BEST describes "stockout cost"?
options: The cost of placing a purchase order
The cost of holding excess inventory in the warehouse
The cost of lost sales, backorders, and customer dissatisfaction from inventory shortages
The transportation cost of emergency shipments

questionText: In probabilistic inventory models, increasing the desired service level will generally:
options: Decrease the required safety stock
Increase the required safety stock
Have no effect on safety stock
Reduce the reorder point

questionText: Which of the following is used to manage a large number of independent demand items with lower monitoring cost?
options: MRP system
Continuous review with individual reorder points for each item
ABC analysis combined with differentiated review systems
Just-in-time delivery from all suppliers

questionText: The "Type I service level" in inventory management is defined as:
options: The fraction of demand satisfied from stock on hand
The probability of not stocking out during a single replenishment cycle
The ratio of orders filled on time to total orders
The percentage of items maintained above the reorder point

questionText: The "Type II service level" (fill rate) measures:
options: The probability of no stockout per replenishment cycle
The fraction of total demand satisfied without backorders
The number of orders placed per year without shortage
The ratio of safety stock to average cycle stock

questionText: Which of the following will REDUCE the reorder point in a probabilistic demand model?
options: Increase in average lead time
Increase in demand variability
Reduction in desired service level
Increase in average daily demand

questionText: Which inventory model is most appropriate when demand is uncertain and items are sold directly to end consumers?
options: Basic EOQ with constant demand
Production Order Quantity model
Probabilistic independent demand model
MRP-based dependent demand model

questionText: Which of the following statements correctly describes the relationship between lead time variability and safety stock?
options: Higher lead time variability requires lower safety stock
Lead time variability has no effect on safety stock
Higher lead time variability requires higher safety stock
Safety stock is determined only by demand variability, not lead time

questionText: A company wants to achieve a 99% service level. Compared to a 90% service level, this will require:
options: Less safety stock and a lower reorder point
More safety stock and a higher reorder point
The same safety stock but a lower reorder point
More safety stock but the same reorder point

questionText: In the context of independent demand inventory systems, "lost sale" refers to:
options: A sale that was recorded incorrectly in the inventory system
Demand that is permanently lost because the item was out of stock
A purchase order that was cancelled by the supplier
Inventory that was damaged and written off

questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of "C" items under ABC analysis?
options: They represent a small number of SKUs with high annual value
They represent the largest number of SKUs but the smallest share of total value
They require the tightest inventory controls and most frequent reviews
They are typically managed with continuous review systems

questionText: Which of the following best describes "vendor-managed inventory" (VMI) in the context of independent demand?
options: The buyer manages all inventory replenishment decisions independently
The supplier takes responsibility for monitoring and replenishing the buyer's inventory
A third-party logistics provider manages inventory for both buyer and supplier
Inventory management is outsourced to a government agency

questionText: A retail store maintains safety stock for a fast-moving consumer good. Which factor most directly determines the required safety stock level?
options: The unit purchase price of the item
Variability in demand and supplier lead time
The physical size of the item's storage location
The number of competing products in the same category

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes "obsolescence risk" in inventory management?
options: The risk of receiving defective goods from suppliers
The risk that inventory will lose value or become unsalable before it is used or sold
The risk of stockouts during the lead time period
The risk of supplier price increases affecting holding costs

questionText: Dependent demand items are characterized by demand that is:
options: Driven by external customers purchasing finished goods
Derived from the production requirements of a parent or finished item
Forecasted independently using time series methods
Managed through continuous review reorder point systems

questionText: Which of the following is the primary tool used to manage dependent demand inventory?
options: Economic Order Quantity (EOQ)
Periodic review system
Material Requirements Planning (MRP)
ABC analysis

questionText: In MRP, the "Master Production Schedule" (MPS) serves as:
options: A record of current on-hand inventory for all items
The primary input that drives all lower-level material requirements
A tool for evaluating supplier performance
A forecast of independent demand for raw materials

questionText: The "Bill of Materials" (BOM) in MRP is:
options: A financial statement of inventory costs
A structured list of all components and quantities needed to produce one unit of a parent item
A supplier catalog listing prices and lead times
A warehouse location guide for all inventory items

questionText: MRP "netting" refers to the process of:
options: Calculating the total ordering cost for all materials
Subtracting on-hand inventory and scheduled receipts from gross requirements to determine net requirements
Grouping similar items together for combined purchase orders
Allocating warehouse space based on item volume

questionText: In MRP, "gross requirements" represent:
options: The total quantity of an item needed before considering on-hand inventory
The quantity to be ordered after accounting for current stock
The maximum inventory level for an item
The total cost of all materials in the BOM

questionText: Which of the following is an input to the MRP system?
options: Finished goods selling price
Customer satisfaction surveys
On-hand inventory records
Annual financial statements

questionText: "Lot sizing" in MRP determines:
options: The physical dimensions of each inventory item
The quantity to order or produce in each time period
The number of suppliers needed for each component
The warehouse location for each item

questionText: The "time bucket" in MRP planning refers to:
options: The storage container used for small components
The discrete time period (e.g., week) used to organize the MRP schedule
The lead time for the longest-lead item in the BOM
The time required to process a customer order

questionText: "Planned order release" in MRP means:
options: An order that has already been sent to the supplier
An order that MRP has scheduled to be released in a future time period
An order that was released in a previous planning period
An order that was cancelled due to demand changes

questionText: Which of the following best describes "scheduled receipts" in MRP?
options: Orders that have already been placed and are expected to arrive
Finished goods scheduled for delivery to customers
Inventory that has been physically received and counted
Production orders that have been completed in the current period

questionText: The MRP system calculates the "planned order release" date by:
options: Adding the lead time to the date net requirements are needed
Subtracting the lead time from the date net requirements are needed
Multiplying the lot size by the lead time
Dividing net requirements by the average daily demand

questionText: Which of the following is a limitation of MRP systems?
options: They cannot handle multi-level BOMs
They assume infinite production capacity which may not reflect reality
They are unable to calculate net requirements
They cannot integrate with master production schedules

questionText: MRP II (Manufacturing Resource Planning) extends MRP by incorporating:
options: Only inventory management functions
Financial, human resources, and capacity planning in addition to material planning
Qualitative demand forecasting methods
Customer relationship management exclusively

questionText: Which of the following describes "pegging" in MRP?
options: The process of fixing order quantities to supplier minimum quantities
The ability to trace net requirements back to the parent demand that caused them
Linking inventory records to warehouse bin locations
Assigning priority to production orders based on due dates

questionText: "Explosion" in the context of MRP refers to:
options: A sudden increase in demand that overwhelms the inventory system
The process of extending the MPS through the BOM to calculate all component requirements
A rapid deterioration of inventory quality
An unexpected increase in supplier lead time

questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of MRP over independent demand models for managing component parts?
options: MRP requires less data input and is easier to administer
MRP explicitly links component requirements to parent item production schedules
MRP eliminates the need for safety stock at all levels
MRP uses simpler lot sizing rules than EOQ-based systems

questionText: In MRP, the "low-level code" of an item refers to:
options: The item's priority ranking in ABC analysis
The lowest level in the BOM at which the item appears
The minimum order quantity allowed by the supplier
The item's location code in the warehouse system

questionText: Which of the following best describes "nervousness" in MRP systems?
options: The tendency of MRP to generate excessively large safety stocks
Frequent and significant changes in planned orders caused by small changes in the MPS
Inability of MRP to handle changes in the Bill of Materials
Errors caused by inaccurate inventory records in the MRP database

questionText: Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems relate to MRP in that ERP:
options: Replaces MRP with a purely financial planning system
Integrates MRP with other business functions such as finance, HR, and sales
Eliminates the need for a Bill of Materials in manufacturing
Focuses exclusively on customer order management

questionText: Which of the following is required to calculate net requirements in MRP?
options: Selling price, gross profit, and tax rate
Gross requirements, on-hand inventory, and scheduled receipts
EOQ, holding cost, and ordering cost
Safety stock, reorder point, and lead time only

questionText: A company produces a finished product that requires 3 units of component X per unit. If the MPS calls for 200 units of the finished product in Week 5, the gross requirement for component X in Week 5 is:
options: 67 units
200 units
400 units
600 units

questionText: Which of the following best describes "safety time" in MRP, as opposed to safety stock?
options: Scheduling orders to arrive earlier than needed to buffer against demand uncertainty
Adding extra units to planned order quantities to buffer against supply uncertainty
Extending lead time estimates to account for supplier unreliability
Adding a fixed number of units to each order regardless of demand variability

questionText: Which of the following is TRUE about dependent demand compared to independent demand?
options: Dependent demand must be forecasted using time series methods
Dependent demand is more uncertain and unpredictable than independent demand
Dependent demand is calculated directly from parent item requirements, not forecasted independently
Dependent demand items are always managed using EOQ-based systems

questionText: A two-level BOM consists of a finished product at Level 0 and its components at Level 1. If the finished product has a lead time of 2 weeks and a component has a lead time of 3 weeks, what is the minimum total lead time to produce the finished product from scratch?
options: 2 weeks
3 weeks
5 weeks
6 weeks

questionText: Which of the following best distinguishes dependent demand from independent demand?
options: Independent demand is always higher in volume than dependent demand
Independent demand is derived from production schedules; dependent demand is market-driven
Dependent demand is derived from the requirements of parent items; independent demand comes from external customers
Independent demand is managed by MRP; dependent demand is managed by EOQ

questionText: A logistics manager wants to reduce total inventory costs. Which combination of actions is most effective under the EOQ framework?
options: Increase order quantity and increase holding cost
Decrease order quantity and increase ordering frequency
Optimize order quantity at the EOQ level where ordering cost equals holding cost
Eliminate safety stock and reduce the reorder point to zero

questionText: Which of the following inventory performance metrics measures the efficiency of inventory investment?
options: Reorder point
Inventory turnover ratio
Economic order quantity
Mean absolute deviation

questionText: A high inventory turnover ratio indicates:
options: Excess inventory is being carried relative to sales
Inventory is being sold and replaced rapidly, reflecting efficient inventory management
The reorder point is set too high
Safety stock levels are excessive

questionText: Which of the following supply chain events would most likely cause a sudden increase in safety stock requirements?
options: Demand becomes perfectly stable and predictable
A key supplier reduces its lead time significantly
Lead time variability from a major supplier increases substantially
The company implements vendor-managed inventory with all suppliers

questionText: Which of the following best describes the relationship between forecast accuracy and inventory levels?
options: Better forecast accuracy leads to higher safety stock requirements
Poor forecast accuracy increases the need for safety stock to maintain service levels
Forecast accuracy has no impact on safety stock or inventory levels
Higher forecast accuracy always results in higher reorder points

questionText: A company adopts a JIT (Just-in-Time) inventory system. Which of the following outcomes is most expected?
options: Significant increase in warehouse storage requirements
Higher safety stock levels across all inventory categories
Reduction in inventory holding costs and waste
Increased reliance on large, infrequent orders from suppliers

questionText: Which of the following correctly describes the role of inventory management in supply chain coordination?
options: Inventory management operates in isolation from other supply chain functions
Effective inventory management decouples supply chain stages and buffers against variability
Inventory management focuses exclusively on minimizing the number of suppliers
Inventory management is only relevant for manufacturing companies, not service organizations

questionText: A supply chain manager notices that upstream suppliers are holding significantly more inventory than downstream retailers require. This situation most likely reflects:
options: Excellent demand forecasting by all supply chain members
The bullwhip effect causing demand signal amplification upstream
A successful implementation of vendor-managed inventory
Optimal lot sizing decisions by all supply chain participants

questionText: Which of the following is the MOST comprehensive approach to managing inventory across a supply chain?
options: Each company independently minimizes its own inventory costs using EOQ
Applying ABC analysis uniformly to all items across all companies in the chain
Integrating demand information, collaborative forecasting, and synchronized replenishment across all supply chain partners
Centralizing all inventory at a single warehouse to reduce holding costs
